## Summary

Rajeev opened by telling Eric that from today the team runs everyone's update
off the Jira board, and shared his screen so the board drove the round.

Pankaj said his update does not map cleanly to Jira yet. GitHub repo setup is
done: PR checks, security settings around the branch, and a Git flow branch
strategy for cutting branches during development. He was unblocked by Eric
upgrading the GitHub team. He also got access to the Apple developer account,
logged in, set up Xcode with a provisioning profile, and can build the app end
to end on his own machine. Rajeev asked him to pull the matching items into
sprint 1, the discovery phase sprint, and mark them done; Pankaj said he would
do it after the call.

Nitish got the API contract and schema PR merged into the meta repo after
Pankaj's review comments. He closed the Aurora-gate ticket in sprint 1 as
discussed, and will put a comment on SCRIBL-16 and close it too. He started
today on the data model, SCRIBL-20 and SCRIBL-12, which still needs review from
Pankaj and more review iterations. He is off tomorrow for a holiday. No
blockers.

Pramod told Eric the likely cause of the AWS gap: Eric probably created the IAM
roles while still in the original management account view, without switching
into the newly created account, so the roles are tied to the wrong place. If
switching does not fix it, create a temporary user and the DevOps engineer can
look. Pramod then asked Eric, on Karuna's behalf, whether Scribl has a
BrowserStack account for testing across browser, version and mobile
combinations; Eric will send a screenshot of the five accounts under their root
account. Pramod gave advance warning that the QA team will need a Linux EC2
instance once the AWS account is live, to hold the test repository and run
automated tests, and said they will run it past Eric before creating it.

Rob finished pushing the remaining epics and user stories into the backlog
yesterday. This morning Pankaj reviewed and merged his harness PR, which Rob
marked as SCRIBL-4, and he already had the POC in line with the MVP minus the
designs. He asked Eric for a timeline from Christina on the designs; that is
Christina Strachoff, the client-side designer. The transcript has a gap between
10:46 and 11:07 and Rob's question plus part of the answer fall inside it. What
survives is the tail: Rob saying "yes, yes, the shape review" and Eric saying
he could bring the designs up then and finalize deliverables, and that "it's
looking good". Treat the design timeline as raised and pointed at the shape
review, not as answered with a date. Pankaj asked Rob to add an app icon to the
list; Rob thinks one already exists and will double check.

Shubhankar picked SCRIBL-18, assigned himself a few more items, and commented
on SCRIBL-18, which is almost complete. His dev tools are installed, he can run
the app, and he now has GitHub access and can see the code. He is
cross-checking the meta repo against the development done so far to find gaps,
and will create subtasks for the gaps he identifies so he can pick them up
individually.

Karuna is analysing requirements. She went through workflows 1 and 2 and user
story SCRIBL-28, has questions and a working understanding, and will generate
test cases from them. In parallel she is working the automation execution plan
the team discussed earlier that day.

On schedule, Rajeev confirmed with Rob and Eric that the discovery phase
concludes today or tomorrow, and that the next sprint starts Monday and runs to
18 September. It is the first sprint after discovery but the Jira board labels
it sprint 2. Half the team is out tomorrow, 2026-09-04, for a holiday, so
standup is reduced, which Rob flagged to Eric. Monday 2026-09-07 is US Labor
Day. Rob did not know he had it off and said he will not be there. Rajeev first
proposed holding a regular standup Monday because he is out tomorrow, then took
Eric's likely absence into account and landed on the India team connecting
internally on Monday and everyone reconvening Tuesday. Rob will invite Eric to
the Jira board around the middle of next week, once the team has absorbed the
backlog he pushed yesterday.

## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- From today, team updates run off the Jira board rather than free-form status. Rajeev shared the board on screen and drove the round from it (owner: Rob Forshier II, announced by Rajeev Kumar; the change was settled in the grooming session that ran immediately before this call).
- The app repo uses a Git flow branch strategy, with PR checks and branch security rules now in place (owner: Pankaj Aggarwal).
- The Aurora-gate ticket in sprint 1 is closed as discussed, so the database decision is no longer open work (owner: Nitish Goyal).
- Discovery concludes today or tomorrow, and the next sprint runs Monday 2026-09-07 to 18 September. It is the first development sprint but appears on the Jira board as sprint 2 (owner: Rajeev Kumar, confirmed with Rob Forshier II and Eric Rice).
- No full standup on Monday 2026-09-07. The India team connects internally and everyone reconvenes Tuesday 2026-09-08. Rajeev initially proposed a regular Monday standup; the final state is the Tuesday plan (owner: Rajeev Kumar, agreed by Eric Rice: "OK, let's do that").
- Tomorrow's standup, 2026-09-04, runs with a reduced group because half the team is out for a holiday (owner: Rob Forshier II).

- When will Christina Strachoff deliver the designs? Rob asked Eric for a timeline. The question and part of the answer sit in a transcript gap between 10:46 and 11:07; what survives is Eric pointing at the shape review and saying it is looking good, with no date (raised by Rob Forshier II, unresolved).
